tests.title: RetryAfter reads Retry-After first, then a reset timestamp, adding one second in each case
given: a rate-limited HTTPError (429, and 403 with RateLimitRemaining "0")
a clock reading roughly now
tests.when: RetryAfter() is called with Retry-After "30"; with RateLimitReset 45 seconds in the future; with a RateLimitReset already in the past; and with both Retry-After "30" and a reset 600 seconds away
then: Retry-After "30" yields (31s, true)
a reset 45 seconds ahead yields a duration of 46s within one second, and true
a reset in the past yields (1s, true) rather than a negative or zero duration
with both present Retry-After wins: the result is 31s, not 601s — and no two-minute ceiling is applied (a Retry-After of 300 yields 301s, true)
tests.pseudocode:
e = func(h map) *HTTPError { return &HTTPError{Status:429, RetryAfterHeader:h.ra, RateLimitReset:h.reset} }
d, ok = e({ra:'30'}).RetryAfter(); assert ok and d == 31*time.Second
d, ok = e({reset: str(now+45)}).RetryAfter(); assert ok and abs(d - 46*time.Second) <= time.Second
d, ok = e({reset: str(now-120)}).RetryAfter(); assert ok and d == 1*time.Second
d, ok = e({ra:'30', reset: str(now+600)}).RetryAfter(); assert ok and d == 31*time.Second
d, ok = e({ra:'300'}).RetryAfter(); assert ok and d == 301*time.Second
d, ok = (&HTTPError{Status:403, RateLimitRemaining:'0', RetryAfterHeader:'30'}).RetryAfter(); assert ok and d == 31*time.Second
